title: Week in Orbit
summary: This week, the space industry is grappling with a mix of operational hiccups and strategic partnerships. SpaceX remains a focal point, both for its ambitious launches and the occasional setbacks that come with them.

themes.title: SpaceX's Launch Challenges
themes.body: SpaceX's abort of the Starship Flight 13 launch attempt underscores the complexities of pushing the envelope in aerospace. Meanwhile, the company continues to expand its military satellite offerings, indicating a dual focus on innovation and reliability.

themes.title: International Agreements on Space
themes.body: Serbia's signing of the Artemis Accords signals a growing trend of nations aligning with U.S. space policy. This could pave the way for increased collaboration in lunar exploration and beyond, though the real impact remains to be seen.

themes.title: Defense Budget Increases
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup's addition of $1.4 billion to space resilience reflects a heightened focus on national security in the face of evolving threats. This funding boost may bolster various initiatives, including missile defense tracking systems.

themes.title: Emerging Technologies in Space
themes.body: The partnership between Anduril and L3Harris for a tactical SDA constellation highlights the increasing reliance on advanced technologies for space domain awareness. As threats evolve, such collaborations will be crucial in maintaining strategic advantages.
